profile.campus: Suwanee, Gwinnett County, Georgia (QTS Suwanee campus, QTS operations support center)
profile.reading:
Per QTS's own site, Suwanee DC1 sits at 300 Satellite Blvd NW, Suwanee, GA 30024, part of a 53-acre campus with 50+ MW critical capacity currently, with 100+ MW planned; QTS's own site also lists an operations support center in Suwanee, making this a company operational hub beyond pure colocation.

QTS was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas, and was taken private in a roughly $10 billion Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT)-led acquisition completed August 31, 2021, per Blackstone's own press release; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer. QTS's own site lists an operations support center in Suwanee, Georgia, making this Atlanta-metro cluster (Atlanta proper, Suwanee/Gwinnett County, and Fayetteville/Fayette County) an operationally significant hub for the company beyond its Northern Virginia headquarters.

Georgia Power, the state's dominant investor-owned electric utility, has flagged data center load growth in its own integrated resource plan filings with state regulators as a major driver of future generation and transmission investment, a pattern also seen among Northern Virginia's Dominion Energy and Texas's ERCOT grid operator elsewhere in this registry. Metro Atlanta's data center growth has also drawn legislative attention over sales-tax exemptions for data center equipment, a policy debate covered in Georgia trade and political press as the industry has expanded across Fulton, Gwinnett, Fayette, and neighboring counties.

QTS positions itself as a "hyperscale-neutral" wholesale and colocation landlord, leasing built capacity to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale tenants rather than operating its own end-user cloud service, a business model shared with peers like Digital Realty and CyrusOne, both also present in the metro Atlanta market. Under Blackstone ownership since 2021, QTS has continued expanding its Georgia footprint, including the still-under-development Fayetteville mega-campus tracked elsewhere in this registry, rather than slowing investment after going private.

reading.body:
QTS Suwanee Data Center 1 is part of a 53-acre campus in Gwinnett County with 50+ MW of critical capacity today and 100+ MW planned. If the planned expansion reaches completion, this single campus would represent roughly 150% of Georgia's currently published data center capacity of 66.3 MW across four facilities, making it a material concentrator of AI infrastructure in the state. The facility sits in Georgia's Atlanta metro region, where QTS has held operations since its early 2000s acquisition phase.

The campus publishes 50+ MW of existing capacity, which ranks fifth by announced megawatts among Georgia facilities. At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 50 MW of IT load translates to approximately 1,250 racks. The planned doubling to 100+ MW would bring that to 2,500 racks, a scale sufficient to host a substantial model training cluster or distributed inference workload. No certification or tenant information is published for this facility.

Georgia has 33 mapped data center facilities but only four with published capacity figures, making this campus one of very few whose power footprint is documented. The operator, Quality Technology Services, is controlled by Blackstone as of 2021 and operates across multiple states. Whether this campus matters to AI depends on whether the planned expansion proceeds and which tenants it serves, neither of which is published.
